question: Each of the three composition forms already read against measured RNA in the thirteen reader cells (7d's runtime mean, 7d's promoter competition, 7h's multiplicative composition) read WORSE than running no rule at all, while 7's post-hoc information term beat 992 of 1,000 shuffles. Do the compiled rules therefore carry information at the wrong SIZE: with ONE scale per form, fitted on training genes alone and applied to held-out genes, does the scaled run come closer to measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types than the no-rule baseline; and what is that scale?
prior_exposure: STATED PLAINLY, AND NOT A CAVEAT ADDED AFTERWARDS. This measurement is not fresh for this project. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples, under the same log2(TPM+1) endpoint and the same no-rule baseline, has already been read by: item 7 (M2b, lane-readercompile, data/results/readergate_result.json) including its post-hoc information term; item 7d (M2c, lane-combine2) for the runtime's mean and promoter competition; item 7h (M2f, lane-multrna) for the multiplicative composition; and today's capped-sum census (lane-capsumrna), which reached NOT_TESTABLE. The P and D this lane calibrates ARE 7d's and 7h's committed rows, so every value it reads has been read before, and the choice to look for a magnitude at all was made BECAUSE those readings came out worse than no rule. The held-out split limits that exposure and does not eliminate it: the split is fixed before any held-out number is read and no held-out gene enters any fit, but the held-out genes' RNA values were in the earlier readings' populations, the endpoint and baseline were chosen with those readings in hand, and nothing here is a blind prediction of an unseen measurement. Any reading from this lane therefore holds as a statement about THIS measurement and is not independent confirmation of it; a magnitude read here is a hypothesis for a fresh measurement, not a result on one

This is a negative result and is not 'no difference detected'; the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024): better; on genes held out of the fit, the reader-gated run scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes lowered the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types below the no-rule baseline's, so it is closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894] over 108,264 gene-cell pairs, 8,328 genes; control p = 0.000999; fitted scale +0.2146 [98.33% CI +0.2007, +0.2283], one number for the whole form, fitted on 8,181 training genes (106,353 gene-cell pairs) and applied unchanged to the held-out genes; the uncalibrated size 7d and 7h read is 1). carried with every reading: this RNA is not a fresh measurement. not_vacuous: a scale fitted to near 0 makes the calibrated prediction near-identical to the no-rule baseline, so its held-out Delta MSE comes out near 0 and the interval straddles 0. A dead scale can therefore MANUFACTURE A STRADDLE but it cannot manufacture a win: a held-out interval wholly above 0 requires the scaled prediction to lower the squared error on genes that entered no fit, which a prediction shrunk to nothing cannot do. 'better' is the one reading the vacuity trap cannot fake, which is why the held-out interval decides and the scale interval is what tells a dead-scale straddle (CALIBRATION_REMOVES, a negative) from a live-scale straddle (INCONCLUSIVE)
falsifier: the reading under test is that the compiled rules carry the right information at the wrong size ('right information, wrong size'), which is what 7d's, 7h's and the capped sum's readings beside 7's post-hoc information term suggest. It is FALSIFIED for a form when that form's held-out Delta MSE interval excludes 0 on the BASELINE's side (upper bound < 0, outcome WORSE): with one scale fitted freely on the training genes, the form is still further from measured RNA than running no rule at all, so no single magnitude of it carries the information on held-out genes. An interval straddling 0 falsifies nothing and is read by the scale: CALIBRATION_REMOVES when the scale interval includes 0 (a negative, not a null), INCONCLUSIVE when it excludes 0. An interval excluding 0 on the rules' side (BETTER) is a POSITIVE for that form and is stated as such in the registered words, with PRIOR_EXPOSURE_CLAUSE attached. NOT_VACUOUS states why 'better' is the reading a dead scale cannot fake
prior_exposure_clause: carried with every reading: this RNA is not a fresh measurement. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples under the same endpoint was read by items 7, 7d and 7h and by today's capped-sum census, and the P and D calibrated here are 7d's and 7h's committed rows; the held-out split limits that exposure and does not eliminate it, so a reading here is a statement about this measurement and a hypothesis for a fresh one, not independent confirmation
limitations: independence: each element's removal fold comes from AlphaGenome's RNA-seq gene scorer (an in-silico deletion, the argmax over 371 RNA-seq tracks), a model trained on ENCODE and GTEx RNA-seq, with RNA-seq tracks named for the reader biosamples among them, and on ENCODE DNase-seq; the reader's open/closed calls are ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak files of the same biosamples; the measured outcome is ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of those biosamples, data of the kind, and possibly the very experiments, the model was trained on. The cross-cell pattern of a gated prediction comes from the DNase calls alone and the size of each element's part from the model

PRIOR EXPOSURE, repeated as a limitation because it is the largest one: see PRIOR_EXPOSURE. The held-out genes' RNA values were inside the populations of items 7, 7d, 7h and the capped-sum census, and the decision to look for a magnitude was made because those readings came out worse than no rule. No number here is a blind prediction

one scale is the smallest calibration there is and also the weakest: it can only shrink, grow or flip a form's predictions as a block. It cannot fix a form whose error is in the SHAPE of its prediction across cells or across genes, and a form that reads FURTHER even at its best scale is not thereby shown to carry no information — only that no single magnitude of it helps on these held-out genes

the calibration is a statistical rescaling and not a mechanism: a scale of, say, 0.1 does not say that an element's measured removal fold is ten times too large, because the same number would arise from a prediction that is right on a tenth of the genes and empty on the rest. Nothing here attributes the size to any stage of the compiled pipeline
the three populations differ (4,725, 2,501 and 16,509 genes) and are read separately, as 7d and 7h read them; no scale is compared between forms and no head-to-head is registered here
the P and D are the committed tables' five-decimal roundings, which is why the harness admits TOLERANCE rather than exact equality

this lane's control is a within-gene cell permutation and not 7d's or 7h's shuffled-reader control (CARRIED['note']); their registered control p values are carried as context and are not re-decided here

accessibility near a gene tracks its expression across cell types whatever any compiled rule says; an open element is one a rule may act through, not evidence that it does, and no reading here is evidence of a mechanism

one polyA plus experiment per biosample, from several labs; two of the thirteen are tissues (ovary, testis). Every rate under the run is mouse NIH 3T3 or their genome median; no fold prediction depends on it and no level in molecules per cell is quoted

context_verbatim.seven_d_reading: the runtime's mean: worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.4435 [97.5% CI -0.4843, -0.4085] over 61,425 gene-cell pairs, 4,725 genes; control p = 0.3); the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter): worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.8102 [97.5% CI -0.8994, -0.7252] over 32,513 gene-cell pairs, 2,501 genes; control p = 0.734). Head-to-head over the 2,405 genes in both populations, the promoter-competition form was further from measured RNA than the mean (MSE(mean) - MSE(competition) -0.6944 [95% CI -0.7613, -0.6288]).
context_verbatim.seven_h_reading: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024): worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.5361 [97.5% CI -0.5637, -0.5088] over 214,617 gene-cell pairs, 16,509 genes; control p = 1). Head-to-head over the 2,405 genes in all three populations (31,265 gene-cell pairs), the multiplicative composition was closer to measured RNA than the runtime's mean (MSE(mean) - MSE(multiplicative) +0.04395 [97.5% CI +0.0385, +0.04979]) and closer to measured RNA than the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter) (MSE(competition) - MSE(multiplicative) +0.7383 [97.5% CI +0.6625, +0.8183]).
context_verbatim.note: 7d's and 7h's readings are their own, on the uncalibrated forms, quoted and not re-decided here; their shuffled-reader control is not this lane's control

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
